findings.title: Existing SQL expression tests are left in place and will now fail against the "not implemented" stub
findings.body: This PR makes DB.RunCommands and DB.QueryFramesInto unconditionally return errors.New("not implemented"), which means sql.TablesList (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go) and NewSQLCommand (pkg/expr/sql_command.go) now fail for every input. The repository already contains tests that exercise these paths and expect them to work: pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go calls TablesList with valid SQL and asserts on the returned table names, and pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go calls NewSQLCommand/Execute with valid SQL and asserts successful results. None of these test files are updated, skipped, or removed in this PR, so they will fail with "not implemented" / "error reading SQL command" and turn CI red. The tests should be removed or rewritten in this PR to assert the new disabled behavior.

findings.title: Error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is misleading — the feature is deliberately disabled
findings.body: When a dashboard or alert rule contains a SQL expression, the query now fails with the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented". The feature is in fact implemented but has been intentionally disabled in response to CVE-2024-9264 (RCE/LFI), which is exactly the situation users and support staff will need to understand when previously working SQL expressions start failing. The message text is wrong and will generate confusion; it should say something like "SQL expressions are disabled" (ideally referencing the security advisory) instead of claiming the feature does not exist.
